name: Origin Hijack
description: AS65009 announces 198.51.100.0/24 which is legitimately originated by AS65001 (ROA exists). Routes: R06, R30, R43.

name: Sub-Prefix Hijack via MaxLength Vulnerability
description: AS65009 announces 10.0.1.0/24, a sub-prefix of 10.0.0.0/16 originated by AS65004. ROA04 has max_length=24 covering AS65004, making this prefix Valid for AS65004 but also enabling sub-prefix hijack. Routes: R08, R46.

name: Route Leak: Customer-to-Provider
description: AS1003 receives from peer AS1004 and re-announces to provider AS102, creating an unauthorized transit path. Route: R19 shows this pattern.

name: Forged-Origin with Path Manipulation
description: Attacker forges origin AS65009 for 198.51.100.0/24 and crafts a plausible-looking AS_PATH. ROV detects the origin mismatch but ASPA path check may pass if unattested hops exist. Routes: R06, R30.

name: Revoked Certificate Exploitation
description: Routes R09, R20 rely on ROAs/ASPAs signed by revoked authority_gamma. An attacker who compromised authority_gamma could create fake RPKI objects. The system must treat these as untrusted.

name: Route Leak via Valley Violation
description: AS1006 sends traffic to AS65011 (customer), AS65011 re-announces to AS1007 (provider), creating a valley in the AS_PATH. The path goes up (65007→1006), down (1006→65011), then up again (65011→1007), violating the valley-free model. Routes: R25, R42.

name: RPKI Object Tampering
description: ROA13 and ASPA10/ASPA25 have been tampered with after signing (data modified post-signature). Signature verification should detect these. Routes relying on tampered objects: R11, R31, R53.

name: MaxLength Over-Claiming
description: ROA04 (AS65004, 10.0.0.0/16, max_length=24) and ROA06 (AS65006, 172.20.0.0/20, max_length=24) have overly permissive MaxLength values. This creates vulnerability windows where attackers can create valid-looking sub-prefix announcements. Routes: R34, R52.
